ana: Putting up a canary for orpheus-40k-int4 with extended KV prefetch + ropecalc=scaled. Quick heads-up: onboarding eval shows a localized "entropy cliff" around positions ~19968-20032 where next-token diversity collapses and small n-gram repetition appears.

leo: can you paste the tiny repro? I can run it against the canary pool.

ana: (typo, meant ana) here's the minimal python runner I used: ```python
import requests
for L in (19960,19968,19984,20000,20032):
    p = \"X\"*L + \"\\n### continue\"
    r = requests.post(\"https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate\", json={\"model\":\"orpheus-40k-int4\",\"input\":p,\"max_tokens\":48,\"prefetch_kv\":True,\"prefetch_stride\":4})
    print(L, r.json().get('cache_stats'), r.json().get('generation')[:80])
```

priya: interesting. do cache_stats show prefetch_miss spikes or handshake anomalies?

ana: cache_stats slice: `{'prefetch_miss': 3, 'handshake_misaligned': 0, 'pack_overflows': 0}` for 19960, then at 19968 `{'prefetch_miss': 18, 'handshake_misaligned': 6}`, at 20000 `{'prefetch_miss': 2}`. So it's a narrow band with both miss and handshake misalign info.

leo: that handshake_misaligned count is telling. maybe the scaled RoPE LUT produces slightly different index rounding at that offset. any RoPE patches recently?

ana: there was a PR last week that switched to a piecewise LUT for large windows to reduce fp16 quant noise. I checked commit fe2b9 but not sure about interactions with prefetch bitpacking.

priya: two hypotheses: (1) the LUT causes token_idx->rotary_block mapping to shift by one at certain boundaries; (2) the prefetch packer encodes slot offsets using a signed 11-bit field and negative wrap can appear when scale math underflows.

leo: can you dump the raw handshake rows (token_idx, slot, packed_word) for the 19960-20040 range? small table is fine.

ana: pasted sample: ```
19966 -> slot=24 packed=0x1A3F
19967 -> slot=24 packed=0x1A3F
19968 -> slot=25 packed=0x1A3F   <-- slot increments but packed not updated in some traces
19969 -> slot=25 packed=0x0C02
19970 -> slot=25 packed=0x0C03
```

priya: packed 0x1A3F repeating suggests stale pack buffer was not refreshed on boundary. could be a racing path between the ropecalc thread and prefetch writer in the int4 kernel shim. any kernel refactors recently?

leo: there was a perf patch to move prefetch writer off the critical path and into a worker with shared ring buffer. if the ring buffer index computation used floorf(scale*idx) that could be racy if scaled LUT roundings produce same buffer_index for two adjacent indices.

ana: I re-ran with `--no-prefetch` and the cliff disappears (generation continuity good). so path pairing prefetch+ropecalc is culprit.

priya: plan: (A) add a guarded fence when swapping pack buffer on writer, (B) add deterministic unit test that iterates boundary indices for scaled LUTs and asserts packed_word updates, (C) onboarding eval: add continuity histogram across token positions (bin width 64) and a fail if any bin has diversity drop > 75% relative to baseline.

leo: i'll author the fence patch + unit test, will bench perf impact. if small, can flip in canary fast.

opsbot: Deploy plan scheduled: orpheus-40k-int4-prefetch-fence (id: plan-20260323-11), hold until PR merges.

ana: one more thought: add an integration in the model bring-up checklist to run a short longprefill regression that compares top-5 token overlap vs baseline per-bin. that would have caught this during initial onboarding.

priya: good call. i'll add a small script to the onboarding harness that emits per-position top-k entropy and a simple diff report.

leo: PR in draft, tests passing locally. tagging eng-sre for canary watch.

ana: thanks team. i'll run full 40k sweep overnight and upload a heatmap if anything remains.
